messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: latency_regression alert: hosted/redwood-large p95 > 500ms for 10m. Current p95=1.6s. Severity S2.

Pager Duty: Paging Eli (sre) and backup Tara. Please ack and follow incident runbook.

Eli (sre): ack. I'm taking lead. First pass: any deploys or infra changes in last 30m?

Sam (product): customer telemetry: two enterprise customers reported client-side timeouts; several dev orgs saw high tail latencies. No 5xx surge. I've posted a short status update.

Tara (eng-runtime): pulling traces. Hot span is `kvcache.move_page` inside runtime.attach. Model compute looks steady. p50 from 100ms -> 160ms; p95 from 410ms -> 1.6s. Traces show long syscall-like gaps during page copy.

Ivy (eng-tracing): sample trace snippet (sanitized):
trace=ff22a; spans=[recv, dispatch, kvcache.move_page, memcpy_sys, model.exec, serialize]
kvcache.move_page durations: [300ms, 780ms, 1.1s, 1.5s] (tail)
hosts: node-inf-09, node-inf-14 (kernel=6.2.14)

Ravi (infra): confirming we started a rolling kernel update (6.2.13 -> 6.2.14) targeting inference pool F at 2026-04-21T04:10:00Z. Some hosts updated ~04:22Z.

Eli (sre): initial hypothesis list: 1) kernel memcpy/copy_user regression in 6.2.14 causing long syscall durations - PRIMARY; 2) scheduling/preempt changes in kernel -> more context switches - SECONDARY; 3) runtime regression interacting with kernel - POSSIBLE.

Tara (eng-runtime): I can repro on a canary image with 6.2.14 under KV-heavy load. `strace -T` shows copy-like ops with 0.8-1.2ms durations; same workload on 6.2.13 shows ~0.09ms.

Ivy (eng-tracing): timeline quick draft:
- 2026-04-21T04:09:50Z auto-roller kickoff for pool F
- 2026-04-21T04:22:10Z subset of pool F moved to 6.2.14
- 2026-04-21T04:28:30Z traces with tail begin to appear
- 2026-04-21T04:33:05Z alert threshold crossed
- 2026-04-21T04:35:00Z oncall paged

Eli (sre): mitigation options: A) pause and drain upgraded hosts, B) rollback kernel on a small sample, C) increase capacity on unaffected pools. Which is fastest right now?

Ravi (infra): I can pause the roll and mark pool F hosts as draining. Rolling rollback takes longer (requires manual reimage). I'll start drain immediately.

Artifacts Bot: Notifying teams to collect traces, perf, dmesg; artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/1780011223/. Please upload sanitized logs.

Tara (eng-runtime): running `perf stat` on affected canary under load: context-switches=1,020,100; cpu-migrations=24,800; cycles=10,900,000,000; instructions=3,450,000,000. Context-switches ~4-6x baseline.

Ivy (eng-tracing): matching trace ids to hosts: high confidence that affected traces map to kernel=6.2.14 hosts in pool F. Correlation coefficient high.

Eli (sre): start mitigation: drain initiated 04:38:12Z. We'll shift traffic away from pool F and monitor p95 for 10m. If p95 recovers, keep hosts drained and pause rollout.

Ravi (infra): drain in progress. LB shifted ~70% of traffic within 6m. Full drain expected in ~12m. Paused auto-roll globally.

Tara (eng-runtime): after partial drain p95 reduced to ~460ms within 7 minutes. p50 returned near baseline. Good signal. Collecting `strace -T` and `perf record` from canary for artifacts.

Sam (product): customer update: latency improved for affected customers after mitigation; no critical incidents. Communicating ETA for RCA.

Ivy (eng-tracing): dmesg excerpt from node-inf-09:
[  9876.543210] WARNING: CPU: 1 PID: 28901 at __copy_user_generic_unrolled+0x180/0x2f0
[  9876.543890] soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 20s
[  9876.544100] stack backtrace: ...

Tara (eng-runtime): perf top/ flame snapshot indicates the hot stacks attribute significant time to memcpy and __copy_user. Simplified flame: 55% runtime.kvcache.move_page -> 30% memcpy/__copy_user.

Eli (sre): logging owners for RCA and followups: Ravi=infra (kernel diff + gating), Tara=runtime (repro + mitigations), Ivy=traces/timeline, Sam=customer comms, Eli=SRE follow-up and detection rule.

Ivy (eng-tracing): checklist in-thread:
- [x] alert + page
- [x] traces collected and mapped to hosts
- [x] perf + strace from canary captured
- [x] host dmesg captured
- [x] drain mitigation applied and paused rollout
- [ ] flamegraphs + perf scripts uploaded to artifacts bucket
- [ ] RCA doc draft (owner=Ivy)

Ravi (infra): kernel build diff shows small backported change touching memcpy/layout and a security backport. Opening INFRA-1977 to track patch details and upstream references.

Tara (eng-runtime): short-term runtime mitigation idea: avoid synchronous copying of large KV buffers on the hot path; implement an async attach path or reference-counted zero-copy approach. I'll start a spike and add a regression test.

Eli (sre): update: at 04:52:00Z p95 stabilized to ~430ms after drain. Marking incident mitigated for live traffic. We'll keep collecting artifacts for RCA.

Artifacts Bot: uploaded perf and strace artifacts to s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/1780011223/ (priv). Please add any additional sanitized logs.

Ivy (eng-tracing): I'll assemble the RCA skeleton with timeline, evidence table, hypothesis scoring, and owner actions. Target: initial postmortem draft EOD tomorrow.

Sam (product): preparing internal brief for affected accounts and will link RCA when ready.

Eli (sre): closing active mitigation. Thank you all. If anyone finds additional logs or regressions, drop them into the artifacts bucket and ping this thread. :thumbsup:

Incident Bot: Incident mitigated. RCA thread remains open for follow-up and artifacts.
